286	Weights used in total: Archivo 700, 800; Atkinson 400, 600 (and 700 only if a review asks for it).
287	
288	#### 6. Other scales
289	
290	| Scale | Tokens |
291	|---|---|
292	| Spacing (4 px base) | `--space-1` 0.25rem, `-2` 0.5rem, `-3` 0.75rem, `-4` 1rem, `-5` 1.5rem, `-6` 2rem, `-7` 3rem, `-8` 4rem |
293	| Radius (by hierarchy, not one radius everywhere) | `--radius-control` 0.5rem (inputs, options, days), `--radius-card` 0.875rem (plan cards, panels), `--radius-feature` 1.5rem (recommended card, sheet top corners), `--radius-pill` 999rem (segmented control, chips, badges) |
294	| Border width | `--border-width-hairline` 1px, `--border-width-selected` 2px, `--focus-ring-width` 3px, `--focus-ring-offset` 2px |
295	| Sizes | `--size-target-min` 2.75rem (44 px, BR-11), `--size-option-min` 3rem (48 px rows, Q-13), `--size-icon` 1.25rem, `--size-icon-small` 1rem, `--size-flag-height` 1rem, `--size-content-max` 72rem |
296	| Shadows | `--shadow-panel` (popover and sheet), `--shadow-glow-brand` (recommended and chosen plan), `--shadow-none` |
297	| z-index | `--z-base` 0, `--z-header` 10, `--z-overlay` 1000 (equals the CDK overlay container's own `z-index: 1000`, verified in `@angular/cdk@22.3.0` overlay styles; documented, not overridden) |
298	| Breakpoints (mobile-first, `em` so they follow zoom) | `--breakpoint-sheet` 37.5em (600 px: below it panels are bottom sheets, Q-13; at or above it plans go to two columns), `--breakpoint-wide` 64em (1024 px: three plan columns, wider form) |
299	| Motion | durations and easings: ADR-0013 |
300	
301	#### 7. Icons (C1)
302	
303	- Package: **`@lucide/angular` `1.77.0`**, licence **ISC**, peer `@angular/core >=17.0.0` and
304	  `@angular/common >=17.0.0` (satisfied by 22.3.0), `sideEffects: false`, unpacked 20.9 MB
305	  (registry; npm view, 2026-11-21). Each icon is its own standalone component with an attribute
306	  selector on `<svg>` (`LucideIdCard` → `svg[lucideIdCard]`), imported one by one in the component
307	  that uses it. The icons render through template bindings (`[attr.d]`, `@for`), not `innerHTML`
308	  (packed `fesm2022/lucide-angular.mjs`). With no `title` input the icon gets
309	  `aria-hidden="true"` automatically (`hasA11yProp: title != null` → `aria-hidden`), and we never
310	  pass `title`, so no icon adds accessible text or `textContent` (BR-04).
311	- Icon sizes and colours come from CSS tokens (`width`/`height: var(--size-icon)`,
312	  `color: currentColor`), not from the `size` input.
313	- **Field-key map** (`frontend/src/app/shared/field-icons.ts`, a pure map plus
314	  `iconForField(config)`; names verified as exports of `@lucide/angular@1.77.0`):
315	
316	  | Field key | Icon | Field key | Icon |
317	  |---|---|---|---|
318	  | `documentType` | `LucideIdCard` | `plate` | `LucideRectangleHorizontal` |
319	  | `documentNumber` | `LucideHash` | `make` | `LucideCar` |
320	  | `fullName` | `LucideUser` | `model` | `LucideCarFront` |
321	  | `birthDate` | `LucideCalendar` | `vehicleYear` | `LucideCalendarRange` |
322	  | `city` | `LucideMapPin` | **any other** `text`/`number`/`select`/`date` key | `LucidePencilLine` (default) |
323	  | `checkbox` fields | none | | |
324	
325	- Other icons: help `LucideInfo`, error `LucideCircleAlert`, success and list items
326	  `LucideCircleCheck`, select chevron `LucideChevronDown`, selected option `LucideCheck`, search
327	  `LucideSearch`, close `LucideX`, months `LucideChevronLeft`/`LucideChevronRight`, date button
328	  `LucideCalendarDays`, processing `LucideLoaderCircle`, unknown-country fallback `LucideEarth`,
329	  step indicator `LucideUserRound` / `LucideShieldCheck` / `LucideReceipt`. Avoid
330	  `credit-card`-style names and any class or file named `…card…` in `.ts`/`.html` of files without
331	  the "no se realiza ningún cobro" copy: the US-03-AC-15 guard (`/tarjeta|\bcard\b/i`) would fail.
332	- **Bundle impact, measured** (production build of a copy of `frontend/` at HEAD in a temporary
333	  directory, `@angular/build` 22.3.0; baseline initial `main` 381.44 kB raw / 98.94 kB transfer):
334	  1 icon +11.33 kB raw / +2.26 kB transfer; 22 icons +78.24 kB raw / **+4.20 kB** transfer. Each
335	  icon compiles its own copy of the shared template (about 3.2 kB raw each), which compresses
336	  well. ADR-0012 keeps the initial bundle under the 500 kB warning by lazy-loading step 1.
337	
338	#### 8. Flags
339	
340	Our own SVGs, one standalone component per flag under `frontend/src/app/shared/flags/`, written by
341	hand from the published constructions (no library): Colombia 2:3, three horizontal bands 2:1:1
342	yellow/blue/red; Chile 2:3, two equal bands white over red, a blue square canton the height of the
343	white band, a white five-pointed star centred in the canton on a circle whose diameter is half the
344	canton side (Wikipedia, "Flag of Colombia" and "Flag of Chile", read 2026-11-21; neither law fixes
345	exact colours, so the colour values are the published approximations, ADR-0011). Each is `viewBox`
346	geometry only (`rect`, one `polygon`), fills from component tokens through CSS classes (no hex in
347	templates), `aria-hidden="true"`, `focusable="false"`, no `<title>`, no text; under 1 kB of
348	template each. A 1 px `--color-border-control` ring (4.23:1 on the header) separates the dark blue
349	areas from the near-black background. Where the flags appear and what replaces them for other
350	countries: ADR-0011.
351	
352	### Consequences
353	
354	- Good, because every value has one home and one name; the guard makes "no loose values" a gate
355	  failure, not a review comment (D1), at zero dependency cost (D8).
356	- Good, because the contrast proof is a test over the real token file: a tuned colour that breaks a
357	  pair fails the gate, gradients included (D2).
358	- Good, because the semantic tier isolates components from raw values: a light theme or a palette
359	  change touches `tokens.css` only.
360	- Good, because the icon package is the maintained one, compatible with Angular 22.3.0, hides
361	  icons by default and has no `innerHTML` path (D5, D6); the transfer cost of 22 icons is about
362	  4 kB.
363	- Good, because both fonts are OFL-1.1, same-origin, and the text face is chosen for the exact
364	  data the form collects.
365	- Bad, because a regex-based CSS guard is weaker than a real parser: a construct it does not
366	  anticipate (a value split across lines, an escape) could slip through — mitigation: the style
367	  files are small and simple; the sensitivity self-test covers each rule; the code-reviewer still
368	  reads the CSS; A2 remains the upgrade path.
369	- Bad, because `@lucide/angular` costs about 3.2 kB **raw** per icon (each icon is a component), so
370	  the raw initial size grows faster than the transfer size — mitigation: icons used only on step 1
371	  move to the lazy chunk (ADR-0012); budgets are measured on every build.
372	- Bad, because the Archivo width-axis file is 90 kB, about 55 kB more than its weight-only file
373	  (`archivo-latin-wght-normal.woff2`, 34,928 bytes) — mitigation: not preloaded, `swap`, used only
374	  for headings and prices, cached after the first visit; if HC2 prefers bytes over the width
375	  treatment, switching to the weight-only file is a one-line change.
376	- Bad, because a 3:1 border on every interactive card and input is heavier than the "thin, subtle"
377	  borders of the reference — mitigation: 1 px width, and subtle hairlines stay on non-interactive
378	  panels only (*Spec impact* 2).
379	- Neutral: the dark-only theme means users with a light-mode preference get the dark UI; that is
380	  the brief.
381	
382	### Strongest argument against
383	
384	Stylelint (A2) is the standard tool for exactly this rule: it parses CSS with PostCSS, reports
385	the line and column in the editor while the developer types, has a maintained
386	`declaration-strict-value` plugin, and `stylelint-config-standard` would catch a whole class of
387	other CSS mistakes for free. A home-made regex guard re-implements a parser badly, will drift as
388	the CSS grows, and gives feedback only when the test suite runs. Adding two pinned, MIT-licensed
389	devDependencies is a small price for that.
390	
391	**Why we accept it:** the rule set here is narrow and project-specific (tier prefixes, "no
392	primitive in components", breakpoints that must equal token values, a single declaring file), so
393	Stylelint would need custom rules or plugin configuration for most of it anyway, plus a lint-step
394	change. The repository already enforces ADR rules as Vitest static guards that run in the gate
395	(ADR-0008, ADR-0009), and the sensitivity self-test makes a silent pass visible. If the guard
396	proves brittle during implementation or review, A2 is a contained switch: add the two
397	devDependencies through a superseding note and delete the guard.
398	
399	### Confirmation
400	
401	- `static-guards` / `design-guards` (US-04-AC-01, AC-19, AC-21): the rules of §2; at most two
402	  `@font-face` families, both WOFF2 with `font-display: swap`, `src` same-origin (`/fonts/…`);
403	  `frontend/package.json` versions exact and the dependency names equal the pre-US-04 list plus
404	  exactly `@lucide/angular`, `@fontsource-variable/archivo`,
405	  `@fontsource-variable/atkinson-hyperlegible-next`, and the additions of ADR-0012.
406	- `contrast.spec.ts` (US-04-AC-02): a pure WCAG ratio function with known reference values
407	  (black/white 21, `#777777` on white about 4.48), and every row of `contrast-pairs.json` resolved
408	  from `tokens.css`.
409	- `field-icons.spec.ts` (US-04-AC-04): every key of §7 maps to its icon; an unknown key of each
410	  non-checkbox type gets the default; `checkbox` gets none.
411	- Component tests (AC-04, AC-20): every `svg` in the wizard is `aria-hidden="true"`; accessible
412	  names and `textContent` of the buttons of AC-04 unchanged.
413	- HC3 visual review (AC-23): the look matches §4–§8.
414	
415	## Pros and Cons of the Options
416	
417	### A1. Static guard in Vitest (chosen)
418	
419	- Good, because it runs in the existing gate with no new dependency and follows the repository's
420	  pattern for ADR rules (`static-guards.spec.ts`).
421	- Good, because project-specific rules (tiers, breakpoints equal to tokens, single declaring file)
422	  are a few lines each.
423	- Bad, because it is regex-based (no CSS parser) and reports only at test time.
424	
425	### A2. Stylelint 18.1.0 + `stylelint-declaration-strict-value` 1.13.0
426	
427	Verified on npm (2026-11-21): `stylelint@18.1.0` MIT, 19 direct dependencies;
428	`stylelint-declaration-strict-value@1.13.0` MIT, peer `stylelint >=16 <=18`.
429	
430	- Good, because it is a real parser with editor feedback and a large rule ecosystem.
431	- Bad, because the tier, breakpoint and single-file rules still need custom configuration or a
432	  plugin; two more devDependencies (with their transitive tree) and a lint-step change.
433	
434	### B1. Dark only (chosen)
435	
436	- Good, because it is the brief, halves the contrast rows and the screenshot set.
437	- Bad, because there is no light alternative for people who prefer one.
438	
439	### B2. Dark and light by `prefers-color-scheme`
440	
441	- Good, because it respects the system preference.
442	- Bad, because every AC-02 row and every AC-22 screenshot doubles, and the brief describes only the
443	  dark look; the light palette would be invented, not briefed.
444	
445	### C1. `@lucide/angular` 1.77.0 (chosen)
446	
447	- Good, because it is the Lucide team's current Angular package (the README links a migration guide
448	  from `lucide-angular`), standalone and signal-based, compatible with 22.3.0, ISC.
449	- Good, because rendering uses template bindings only and icons are hidden by default.
450	- Bad, because each icon is a compiled component: +78.24 kB raw for 22 icons (measured).
451	
452	### C2. `@ng-icons/core` 36.1.0 + `@ng-icons/lucide` 36.1.0
453	
454	Verified: `@ng-icons/core` MIT, peer `@angular/core >=22.0.0`; `@ng-icons/lucide` ISC.
455	
456	- Good, because one generic component and SVG strings make it small: +13.27 kB raw / +2.50 kB
457	  transfer for the same 22 icons (measured).
458	- Bad, because it inserts the SVG string with `innerHTML` (`fesm2022/ng-icons-core.mjs:458`, `:486`)
459	  inside the library. Our guard would not see it, but it is the exact path ADR-0009 and spec §9
460	  rule out for icons.
461	- Bad, because icons are registered and referenced by string name (`name="lucideIdCard"`), so a typo
462	  is a runtime blank, not a compile error; two packages to keep in step.
463	
464	### C3. `lucide-angular` 1.0.0 (the name in the story)
465	
466	- Bad, because it is **deprecated** ("Package deprecated. Please use @lucide/angular instead.",
467	  `npm view lucide-angular deprecated`), its last release is 1.0.0 (2026-03-23), and its peer range
468	  is `@angular/core 13.x - 21.x`: `npm install -E lucide-angular@1.0.0` against the project's
469	  dependencies fails with `ERESOLVE` (reproduced in a temporary copy). Not viable without
470	  `--legacy-peer-deps`, which CLAUDE.md §4 pinning does not allow us to paper over.
471	
472	### D1. Archivo + Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (chosen)
473	
474	- Good, because each face has a job tied to this product: legibility of IDs and plates; a width
475	  axis for the display treatment the brief asks for.
476	- Good, because both are OFL-1.1 variable fonts with a Latin subset that covers Spanish.
477	- Bad, because the display file is 90 kB.
478	
479	### D2. One family (Atkinson Hyperlegible Next only)
480	
481	- Good, because it is the lightest (34 kB) and the most consistent.
482	- Bad, because the brief's "large bold display headings" would rely on size alone; the skill and
483	  the brief both ask for a type treatment with character, and the face has no width axis.
484	
485	### D3. "Sora" or "Space Grotesk" + "Inter" (the spec's starting candidates)
486	
487	- Good, because they are popular, well-hinted and available on Fontsource.
488	- Bad, because they are the families any generated UI reaches for; the vendored `frontend-design`
489	  skill asks to choose typefaces "deliberately, not the default families" (CLAUDE.md §5 adopts the
490	  skill with overrides that do not touch this rule), and neither is chosen for this product's
491	  data.
492	
493	## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)
494	
495	1. **US-04-Q-09** names `lucide-angular` (ISC) as the default. That package is deprecated and does
496	   not install against Angular 22.3.0; the chosen package is **`@lucide/angular` 1.77.0**. The map
497	   in Q-09 is kept with Lucide component names (§7).
498	2. **US-04-AC-02** row "input and card border, 3:1": this ADR reads "card" as an **interactive**
499	   card (plan cards, which are pointer targets). Non-interactive panels (summary sections) keep a
500	   decorative hairline below 3:1, which WCAG 1.4.11 allows. The human confirms at HC1/HC2.
501	3. **US-04-BR-12** "at most the weights the type scale uses": with variable fonts there is one file
502	   per family covering a range; the rule is met by limiting the `font-weight` descriptor to the
503	   used range (§5). **US-04-AC-19** "two families plus a generic fallback": the fallback stack
504	   names local system fonts that are never downloaded; the guard counts `@font-face` families.
505	4. **US-04-Q-08** candidates are replaced by §5.
506	5. **US-04-Q-03** starting values are replaced by §4 (and ADR-0011 for the accents).
507	6. Spec §8 mentions a "Seleccionado" badge on the chosen plan, but §8.1 does not list that string.
508	   Either add it to §8.1 or drop the badge (the native radio state plus border and glow already
509	   show the choice).
510	
511	## More Information
512	
513	- **Verified on 2026-11-21** (npm registry with `npm view`, packages fetched with `npm pack` into a
514	  temporary directory, and a production build of a copy of `frontend/` in a temporary directory;
515	  nothing installed in the project):
516	  - `@lucide/angular@1.77.0`: ISC, peers `>=17.0.0`, `sideEffects: false`, dist-tag `latest`;
517	    `lucide-angular`: latest `1.0.0`, deprecated, peers `13.x - 21.x`, `ERESOLVE` against 22.3.0.
518	  - `@ng-icons/core@36.1.0` MIT, `@ng-icons/lucide@36.1.0` ISC.
519	  - `@fontsource-variable/archivo@5.3.0` and `@fontsource-variable/atkinson-hyperlegible-next@5.3.0`:
520	    OFL-1.1; file sizes above from the packed `files/` directories; axes from `metadata.json`.
521	  - `stylelint@18.1.0` MIT; `stylelint-declaration-strict-value@1.13.0` MIT.
522	  - Build measurements (raw / estimated transfer of initial `main`): baseline 381.44 / 98.94 kB;
523	    +1 Lucide icon 392.77 / 101.20; +22 Lucide icons 459.68 / 103.14; +22 icons via `@ng-icons`
524	    394.71 / 101.44.
525	  - Contrast numbers: computed with a throwaway Node script (OKLCH → sRGB with Ottosson's matrices,
526	    gamut-mapped by chroma reduction; WCAG 2.x relative luminance). The production test recomputes
527	    them from `tokens.css`.
528	- **Credit:** OKLCH ramps, "3:1 for controls, icons and focus indicators" and "reduced motion
529	  reduces movement, not feedback" are restated from `pbakaus/impeccable` at `0a4e72a`
530	  (`colorize.md`, `animate.md`; Apache-2.0), as EVAL-004 allows; no file was copied.
531	- **Skill conflicts (CLAUDE.md §1, §5):** the `frontend-design` skill lists a near-black background
532	  with one accent and gradient-washed cards among generated defaults; the brief asks for exactly
533	  that look, so the brief wins (§5 override). The skill's "spend your boldness in one place" is
534	  applied: the recommended plan card (gradient and glow) and the display type are the two loud
535	  elements; everything else is quiet.
536	- **Related ADRs:** ADR-0011 (country visuals, amends ADR-0001), ADR-0012 (select and date picker,
537	  amends ADR-0004; lazy step 1), ADR-0013 (motion tokens and reduced motion), ADR-0009 (no
538	  `innerHTML`; heading levels), ADR-0002 (same origin only).
539	- **Revisit when:** a light theme is requested; the CSS guard misses a real violation in review;
540	  `@lucide/angular` changes its rendering to `innerHTML` or drops Angular 22 from its peers; the
541	  initial bundle passes the 500 kB warning even with step 1 lazy.

consulted: specs/US-04/story.md, specs/US-04/spec.md v0.1 (Draft; §4 BR-01..BR-04, BR-12, BR-14, §5 AC-01, AC-02, AC-04, AC-19, AC-21, AC-23, §6 Q-01, Q-03, Q-08, Q-09, Q-10, §9), docs/qa/US-04/before/, frontend/src (styles.css, component styles, static-guards.spec.ts, angular.json budgets, nginx/default.conf.template), vendored frontend-design skill (EVAL-005, with the CLAUDE.md §5 overrides), principles of pbakaus/impeccable restated with credit (EVAL-004), npm registry and packed packages (@lucide/angular 1.77.0, lucide-angular 1.0.0, @ng-icons/core and @ng-icons/lucide 36.1.0, @fontsource-variable/archivo and @fontsource-variable/atkinson-hyperlegible-next 5.3.0, stylelint 18.1.0, stylelint-declaration-strict-value 1.13.0), a throwaway production build of a copy of frontend/ in a temporary directory, a contrast script (WCAG 2.x relative luminance)
informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence; test-engineer (AC-01, AC-02, AC-04, AC-19, AC-21 guards read the files named here); frontend-developer

# ADR-0010: Design tokens and visual language (theme, palette, type, scales, icons, flags)

## Context and Problem Statement

US-04 redesigns every page of the wizard on a tokenized design system (`specs/US-04/spec.md` §1,
BR-01..BR-04, BR-12). Today the front end has twelve colour custom properties in `styles.css`
and literal lengths, colours and fonts spread over six component style files. The story asks for
tokens in one file in three tiers with no loose values in components, AA contrast proven over
gradients and a dotted texture, two self-hosted font families, one icon library imported icon by
icon, and flags. The human's visual direction (spec "Sources") pins the look: a deep near-black
background with a subtle dotted texture, a violet/indigo accent, a recommended plan card with a
vertical violet gradient and a soft glow, rounded cards with thin borders, pill segmented
controls, check-circle icons in lists, large bold display headings and high-contrast light
primary buttons. The story's first deliverable is this proposal with an example palette and type
scale (story, "First deliverable"). This ADR decides the token architecture and how it is
enforced, the theme (US-04-Q-01), the palette and its contrast proof (Q-03), the type (Q-08), the
scales, the icon library and field-key map (Q-09) and the flag assets (Q-10). Where the flags and
the per-country accent come from, and how that squares with ADR-0001, is ADR-0011.

## Decision Drivers

- D1. One token file, three tiers, no loose values in components, checked automatically
  (US-04-BR-01, US-04-AC-01; CLAUDE.md §9: "checked mechanically").
- D2. WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text, UI component boundaries, focus indicators and
  meaningful icons, at every gradient stop and over the texture (US-04-BR-02, US-04-AC-02; story
  rules "AA contrast"). The pair list must be machine-readable so the test does not guess (AC-02
  note).
- D3. The human's visual direction above is the brief. CLAUDE.md §5 (`frontend-design`
  overrides): "the brief's words win, including when the approved direction matches one of the
  skill's generated defaults"; no aesthetic risk beyond the accepted ADR; the wizard is a task flow.
- D4. At most two font families, self-hosted, WOFF2, `font-display: swap`, at most the weights the
  type scale uses, no third-party origin at runtime (US-04-BR-12, US-04-AC-19; ADR-0002: the
  browser talks only to its own origin).
- D5. One icon library, icons imported one by one, no icon font, no runtime fetch, decorative icons
  hidden; exact version, permissive licence, compatible with `@angular/core` 22.3.0 (US-04-BR-04,
  BR-14; CLAUDE.md §4).
- D6. No `innerHTML` anywhere in the front end (ADR-0009; `static-guards.spec.ts`, US-03-AC-13;
  spec §9 "no `innerHTML` for icons or flags").
- D7. Bundle budgets of `angular.json` (initial 500 kB warning / 1 MB error; component style 4 kB
  warning / 8 kB error) are kept or a change is justified (spec §9, Performance).
- D8. Few new dependencies, each pinned exactly, licence reviewed (US-04-BR-14; CLAUDE.md §4).

## Considered Options

Four sub-decisions, each with its own options. The chosen one is marked.

**A. Enforcing "no loose values"**

1. **A1. A static-guard test in Vitest** (chosen) that reads the style files, like the existing
   `static-guards.spec.ts` of ADR-0008 and ADR-0009.
2. **A2. Stylelint** `18.1.0` with `stylelint-declaration-strict-value` `1.13.0` (both MIT), pinned
   devDependencies, run by `npm run lint`.

**B. Theme (US-04-Q-01)**

1. **B1. Dark only** (chosen), `color-scheme: dark`; semantic tokens structured so a light theme can
   be added later by redefining the semantic tier.
2. **B2. Dark and light following `prefers-color-scheme`**, no switch.

**C. Icon library (US-04-Q-09)**

1. **C1. `@lucide/angular` `1.77.0`** (chosen): one standalone component per icon.
2. **C2. `@ng-icons/core` `36.1.0` + `@ng-icons/lucide` `36.1.0`**: one generic `<ng-icon>` and
   icon SVG strings registered by name.
3. **C3. `lucide-angular` `1.0.0`**, the package the story names (verified non-viable, see below).

**D. Font families (US-04-Q-08)**

1. **D1. Archivo (display, width axis) + Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (text)** (chosen).
2. **D2. One family only**: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for everything.
3. **D3. The spec's starting candidates**: "Sora" or "Space Grotesk" + "Inter".

## Decision Outcome

Chosen options: **A1 static guard, B1 dark only, C1 `@lucide/angular@1.77.0`, D1 Archivo +
Atkinson Hyperlegible Next**, because they meet D1–D8 with **three** new runtime dependencies
(one icon package, two font packages) and no new tooling. A1 extends a guard pattern the gate
already runs. B1 is the brief. C1 is the maintained Angular package of the library the story
proposes, renders through template bindings (D6) and hides icons by default. D1 grounds the type
in the subject: plates, RUT and document numbers need unambiguous glyphs, and the display face
comes from a Latin American foundry with a width axis that makes the bold display headings of
the brief a deliberate treatment, not a default.

### What is decided

#### 1. Files and tiers

| File | Holds | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` | Every custom property of the app, the two `@font-face` rules, the `prefers-reduced-motion` and country-accent overrides of tokens (ADR-0011, ADR-0013) | The **only** file that declares a custom property (`--…:`) or `@font-face`. Listed first in `angular.json` `styles`. |
| `frontend/src/styles/contrast-pairs.json` | The AC-02 pair list (format in §4) | Read by the contrast test; never by the app. |
| `frontend/src/styles.css` | Reset, element defaults, focus style, utility classes (`.visually-hidden`) | Semantic and component tokens only. |
| component `*.css` | Component styles | Semantic and component tokens only; no primitive. |

Tier prefixes (the guard keys on them):

| Tier | Prefix | Examples | Who may reference it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primitive | `--primitive-` | `--primitive-violet-400`, `--primitive-ink-950` | `tokens.css` only |
| Semantic | `--color-`, `--font-`, `--text-`, `--leading-`, `--tracking-`, `--weight-`, `--space-`, `--size-`, `--radius-`, `--border-`, `--shadow-`, `--gradient-`, `--texture-`, `--duration-`, `--ease-`, `--z-`, `--breakpoint-`, `--focus-` | `--color-text-muted`, `--space-4`, `--duration-base` | any style file |
| Component | `--component-<name>-` | `--component-button-primary-bg`, `--component-plan-recommended-gradient` | any style file |

Value forms allowed **inside `tokens.css`** (so the contrast test can resolve every pair without
a CSS engine): primitives are 6-digit hex (`#RRGGBB`); a translucent colour is
`color-mix(in srgb, var(--primitive-…) N%, transparent)`; a gradient is
`linear-gradient(<angle>deg, var(--…) P%, …)` or, for the texture only,
`radial-gradient(...)` of one translucent colour token; everything else is a `var()` or a length,
number, duration or `cubic-bezier()`.

#### 2. "No loose values": the static guard (A1)

A Vitest spec (extending `frontend/src/app/static-guards.spec.ts` or a new `design-guards.spec.ts`,
test-engineer's choice) reads every `*.css` under `frontend/src` and asserts, with comments
stripped:

- Only `tokens.css` contains a custom-property declaration or `@font-face`.
- Outside `tokens.css`, no hex colour, `rgb(`/`rgba(`/`hsl(`/`hwb(`/`lab(`/`lch(`/`oklab(`/`oklch(`/
  `color-mix(`, no named colour other than `transparent`, `currentColor`, `inherit` and the
  `forced-colors` system colours (`Canvas`, `CanvasText`, `LinkText`, `Highlight`,
  `HighlightText`, `ButtonText`, `ButtonFace`, `GrayText`); no `font-family` value other than
  `var(--…)` or `inherit`; no `px`/`rem`/`em`/`ch`/`vw`/`vh` length outside `@media`/`@container`
  conditions; no `ms`/`s` duration, `cubic-bezier(`, gradient function, `box-shadow`/`text-shadow`
  literal or numeric `z-index`. Allowed literals: those listed in US-04-BR-01.
- No component style file references `--primitive-`.
- Every length in a `@media`/`@container` condition equals one `--breakpoint-*` value of
  `tokens.css`, and only `min-width` is used (mobile-first, US-04-BR-11), except the
  `prefers-reduced-motion`, `forced-colors` and `prefers-color-scheme` media features.
- A sensitivity self-test: a fixture string with one violation of each kind must be reported
  (the guard must not pass by finding nothing). Same idea as the "the guard looks at something"
  test of US-03-AC-13.

Third-party CSS that Angular libraries inject themselves (the CDK overlay styles, ADR-0012) is not
in `frontend/src` and is out of the guard's scope; our overrides of it live in `styles.css` and
use tokens.

#### 3. Theme (B1)

Dark only. `:root { color-scheme: dark; }`. No `prefers-color-scheme` branch, no switch. The
semantic tier is the only one components see, so a later light theme redefines semantic tokens
in one block of `tokens.css` and needs its own contrast rows; nothing in components changes.

**Machine-readable pair list** (`frontend/src/styles/contrast-pairs.json`): an array of

texture dot colour composited over `--color-bg`. The test resolves names through `var()` chains
in `tokens.css` down to hex and fails if a name does not resolve. Example rows:

```json
[
  { "id": "body-text", "fg": "--color-text", "bg": ["--color-bg", "texture-worst", "--color-surface", "--color-surface-raised", "--color-surface-hover"], "min": 4.5, "ac": "US-04-AC-02" },

]
```

The final hex values may be tuned at implementation; any change must keep every row of the file
passing, and the table above is then regenerated by the test output, not by hand.

### Consequences

- Good, because every value has one home and one name; the guard makes "no loose values" a gate
  failure, not a review comment (D1), at zero dependency cost (D8).
- Good, because the contrast proof is a test over the real token file: a tuned colour that breaks a
  pair fails the gate, gradients included (D2).
- Good, because the semantic tier isolates components from raw values: a light theme or a palette
  change touches `tokens.css` only.
- Good, because the icon package is the maintained one, compatible with Angular 22.3.0, hides
  icons by default and has no `innerHTML` path (D5, D6); the transfer cost of 22 icons is about
  4 kB.
- Good, because both fonts are OFL-1.1, same-origin, and the text face is chosen for the exact
  data the form collects.
- Bad, because a regex-based CSS guard is weaker than a real parser: a construct it does not
  anticipate (a value split across lines, an escape) could slip through — mitigation: the style
  files are small and simple; the sensitivity self-test covers each rule; the code-reviewer still
  reads the CSS; A2 remains the upgrade path.
- Bad, because `@lucide/angular` costs about 3.2 kB **raw** per icon (each icon is a component), so
  the raw initial size grows faster than the transfer size — mitigation: icons used only on step 1
  move to the lazy chunk (ADR-0012); budgets are measured on every build.
- Bad, because the Archivo width-axis file is 90 kB, about 55 kB more than its weight-only file
  (`archivo-latin-wght-normal.woff2`, 34,928 bytes) — mitigation: not preloaded, `swap`, used only
  for headings and prices, cached after the first visit; if HC2 prefers bytes over the width
  treatment, switching to the weight-only file is a one-line change.
- Bad, because a 3:1 border on every interactive card and input is heavier than the "thin, subtle"
  borders of the reference — mitigation: 1 px width, and subtle hairlines stay on non-interactive
  panels only (*Spec impact* 2).
- Neutral: the dark-only theme means users with a light-mode preference get the dark UI; that is
  the brief.

### Strongest argument against

Stylelint (A2) is the standard tool for exactly this rule: it parses CSS with PostCSS, reports
the line and column in the editor while the developer types, has a maintained
`declaration-strict-value` plugin, and `stylelint-config-standard` would catch a whole class of
other CSS mistakes for free. A home-made regex guard re-implements a parser badly, will drift as
the CSS grows, and gives feedback only when the test suite runs. Adding two pinned, MIT-licensed
devDependencies is a small price for that.

**Why we accept it:** the rule set here is narrow and project-specific (tier prefixes, "no
primitive in components", breakpoints that must equal token values, a single declaring file), so
Stylelint would need custom rules or plugin configuration for most of it anyway, plus a lint-step
change. The repository already enforces ADR rules as Vitest static guards that run in the gate
(ADR-0008, ADR-0009), and the sensitivity self-test makes a silent pass visible. If the guard
proves brittle during implementation or review, A2 is a contained switch: add the two
devDependencies through a superseding note and delete the guard.

### Confirmation

- `static-guards` / `design-guards` (US-04-AC-01, AC-19, AC-21): the rules of §2; at most two
  `@font-face` families, both WOFF2 with `font-display: swap`, `src` same-origin (`/fonts/…`);
  `frontend/package.json` versions exact and the dependency names equal the pre-US-04 list plus
  exactly `@lucide/angular`, `@fontsource-variable/archivo`,
  `@fontsource-variable/atkinson-hyperlegible-next`, and the additions of ADR-0012.
- `contrast.spec.ts` (US-04-AC-02): a pure WCAG ratio function with known reference values
  (black/white 21, `#777777` on white about 4.48), and every row of `contrast-pairs.json` resolved
  from `tokens.css`.
- `field-icons.spec.ts` (US-04-AC-04): every key of §7 maps to its icon; an unknown key of each
  non-checkbox type gets the default; `checkbox` gets none.
- Component tests (AC-04, AC-20): every `svg` in the wizard is `aria-hidden="true"`; accessible
  names and `textContent` of the buttons of AC-04 unchanged.
- HC3 visual review (AC-23): the look matches §4–§8.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A1. Static guard in Vitest (chosen)

- Good, because it runs in the existing gate with no new dependency and follows the repository's
  pattern for ADR rules (`static-guards.spec.ts`).
- Good, because project-specific rules (tiers, breakpoints equal to tokens, single declaring file)
  are a few lines each.
- Bad, because it is regex-based (no CSS parser) and reports only at test time.

### A2. Stylelint 18.1.0 + `stylelint-declaration-strict-value` 1.13.0

Verified on npm (2026-11-21): `stylelint@18.1.0` MIT, 19 direct dependencies;
`stylelint-declaration-strict-value@1.13.0` MIT, peer `stylelint >=16 <=18`.

- Good, because it is a real parser with editor feedback and a large rule ecosystem.
- Bad, because the tier, breakpoint and single-file rules still need custom configuration or a
  plugin; two more devDependencies (with their transitive tree) and a lint-step change.

### B1. Dark only (chosen)

- Good, because it is the brief, halves the contrast rows and the screenshot set.
- Bad, because there is no light alternative for people who prefer one.

### B2. Dark and light by `prefers-color-scheme`

- Good, because it respects the system preference.
- Bad, because every AC-02 row and every AC-22 screenshot doubles, and the brief describes only the
  dark look; the light palette would be invented, not briefed.

### C1. `@lucide/angular` 1.77.0 (chosen)

- Good, because it is the Lucide team's current Angular package (the README links a migration guide
  from `lucide-angular`), standalone and signal-based, compatible with 22.3.0, ISC.
- Good, because rendering uses template bindings only and icons are hidden by default.
- Bad, because each icon is a compiled component: +78.24 kB raw for 22 icons (measured).

### C2. `@ng-icons/core` 36.1.0 + `@ng-icons/lucide` 36.1.0

Verified: `@ng-icons/core` MIT, peer `@angular/core >=22.0.0`; `@ng-icons/lucide` ISC.

- Good, because one generic component and SVG strings make it small: +13.27 kB raw / +2.50 kB
  transfer for the same 22 icons (measured).
- Bad, because it inserts the SVG string with `innerHTML` (`fesm2022/ng-icons-core.mjs:458`, `:486`)
  inside the library. Our guard would not see it, but it is the exact path ADR-0009 and spec §9
  rule out for icons.
- Bad, because icons are registered and referenced by string name (`name="lucideIdCard"`), so a typo
  is a runtime blank, not a compile error; two packages to keep in step.

### C3. `lucide-angular` 1.0.0 (the name in the story)

- Bad, because it is **deprecated** ("Package deprecated. Please use @lucide/angular instead.",
  `npm view lucide-angular deprecated`), its last release is 1.0.0 (2026-03-23), and its peer range
  is `@angular/core 13.x - 21.x`: `npm install -E lucide-angular@1.0.0` against the project's
  dependencies fails with `ERESOLVE` (reproduced in a temporary copy). Not viable without
  `--legacy-peer-deps`, which CLAUDE.md §4 pinning does not allow us to paper over.

### D1. Archivo + Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (chosen)

- Good, because each face has a job tied to this product: legibility of IDs and plates; a width
  axis for the display treatment the brief asks for.
- Good, because both are OFL-1.1 variable fonts with a Latin subset that covers Spanish.
- Bad, because the display file is 90 kB.

### D2. One family (Atkinson Hyperlegible Next only)

- Good, because it is the lightest (34 kB) and the most consistent.
- Bad, because the brief's "large bold display headings" would rely on size alone; the skill and
  the brief both ask for a type treatment with character, and the face has no width axis.

### D3. "Sora" or "Space Grotesk" + "Inter" (the spec's starting candidates)

- Good, because they are popular, well-hinted and available on Fontsource.
- Bad, because they are the families any generated UI reaches for; the vendored `frontend-design`
  skill asks to choose typefaces "deliberately, not the default families" (CLAUDE.md §5 adopts the
  skill with overrides that do not touch this rule), and neither is chosen for this product's
  data.

## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)

1. **US-04-Q-09** names `lucide-angular` (ISC) as the default. That package is deprecated and does
   not install against Angular 22.3.0; the chosen package is **`@lucide/angular` 1.77.0**. The map
   in Q-09 is kept with Lucide component names (§7).
2. **US-04-AC-02** row "input and card border, 3:1": this ADR reads "card" as an **interactive**
   card (plan cards, which are pointer targets). Non-interactive panels (summary sections) keep a
   decorative hairline below 3:1, which WCAG 1.4.11 allows. The human confirms at HC1/HC2.
3. **US-04-BR-12** "at most the weights the type scale uses": with variable fonts there is one file
   per family covering a range; the rule is met by limiting the `font-weight` descriptor to the
   used range (§5). **US-04-AC-19** "two families plus a generic fallback": the fallback stack
   names local system fonts that are never downloaded; the guard counts `@font-face` families.
4. **US-04-Q-08** candidates are replaced by §5.
5. **US-04-Q-03** starting values are replaced by §4 (and ADR-0011 for the accents).
6. Spec §8 mentions a "Seleccionado" badge on the chosen plan, but §8.1 does not list that string.
   Either add it to §8.1 or drop the badge (the native radio state plus border and glow already
   show the choice).

## More Information

- **Verified on 2026-11-21** (npm registry with `npm view`, packages fetched with `npm pack` into a
  temporary directory, and a production build of a copy of `frontend/` in a temporary directory;
  nothing installed in the project):
  - `@lucide/angular@1.77.0`: ISC, peers `>=17.0.0`, `sideEffects: false`, dist-tag `latest`;
    `lucide-angular`: latest `1.0.0`, deprecated, peers `13.x - 21.x`, `ERESOLVE` against 22.3.0.
  - `@ng-icons/core@36.1.0` MIT, `@ng-icons/lucide@36.1.0` ISC.
  - `@fontsource-variable/archivo@5.3.0` and `@fontsource-variable/atkinson-hyperlegible-next@5.3.0`:
    OFL-1.1; file sizes above from the packed `files/` directories; axes from `metadata.json`.
  - `stylelint@18.1.0` MIT; `stylelint-declaration-strict-value@1.13.0` MIT.
  - Build measurements (raw / estimated transfer of initial `main`): baseline 381.44 / 98.94 kB;
    +1 Lucide icon 392.77 / 101.20; +22 Lucide icons 459.68 / 103.14; +22 icons via `@ng-icons`
    394.71 / 101.44.
  - Contrast numbers: computed with a throwaway Node script (OKLCH → sRGB with Ottosson's matrices,
    gamut-mapped by chroma reduction; WCAG 2.x relative luminance). The production test recomputes
    them from `tokens.css`.
- **Credit:** OKLCH ramps, "3:1 for controls, icons and focus indicators" and "reduced motion
  reduces movement, not feedback" are restated from `pbakaus/impeccable` at `0a4e72a`
  (`colorize.md`, `animate.md`; Apache-2.0), as EVAL-004 allows; no file was copied.
- **Skill conflicts (CLAUDE.md §1, §5):** the `frontend-design` skill lists a near-black background
  with one accent and gradient-washed cards among generated defaults; the brief asks for exactly
  that look, so the brief wins (§5 override). The skill's "spend your boldness in one place" is
  applied: the recommended plan card (gradient and glow) and the display type are the two loud
  elements; everything else is quiet.
- **Related ADRs:** ADR-0011 (country visuals, amends ADR-0001), ADR-0012 (select and date picker,
  amends ADR-0004; lazy step 1), ADR-0013 (motion tokens and reduced motion), ADR-0009 (no
  `innerHTML`; heading levels), ADR-0002 (same origin only).
- **Revisit when:** a light theme is requested; the CSS guard misses a real violation in review;
  `@lucide/angular` changes its rendering to `innerHTML` or drops Angular 22 from its peers; the
  initial bundle passes the 500 kB warning even with step 1 lazy.

9	# ADR-0012: Accessible custom select and date picker on `@angular/aria` and `@angular/cdk`, bound to Signal Forms (amends ADR-0004)
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	US-04 replaces the browser's `<select>` and `<input type="date">` of step 1 with design-system
14	controls: a select with an icon, search for long lists and the selected option marked, and a date
15	field that accepts typed dd/mm/aaaa and opens a calendar with month and year navigation and days
16	disabled by the `minAge` rule (US-04-BR-05, BR-06). The story requires them to be "built on
17	accessible primitives, not from scratch: Angular CDK (Overlay, Listbox, a11y) or `@angular/aria`
18	if it is stable in our version", with the WAI-ARIA combobox/listbox and date picker dialog
19	patterns, a bottom sheet on mobile, and validations and stored values unchanged. ADR-0004
20	(Accepted) chose Signal Forms with **native controls** (its driver D7) and its implementation note
21	makes `syncNative` the only writer of number and date keys, built on `validity.badInput`. This ADR
22	picks the primitives, defines how the controls plug into Signal Forms and the shared validation
23	core, and amends ADR-0004 where it assumed native controls (US-04-Q-04, Q-05, Q-11..Q-13).
24	
25	## Decision Drivers
26	
27	- D1. WAI-ARIA APG patterns: combobox with listbox popup (select-only and list autocomplete), date
28	  picker dialog; full keyboard map of US-04-AC-06, AC-09; focus trapped and returned; polite
29	  announcements (story; US-04-BR-05, BR-06, BR-13).
30	- D2. Built on primitives, not from scratch; exact versions, permissive licence; `@angular/cdk`
31	  equal to the framework version (story; US-04-BR-14; CLAUDE.md §4).
32	- D3. Same validation, same stored values, same error timing and focus target as before
33	  (US-04-BR-07, AC-11; ADR-0004: string editing model, `validateField` as the only rule engine,
34	  `touched && invalid`, `focusBoundControl()` on a failed submit; ADR-0003 stored shape).
35	- D4. The labelled, focused element is an `<input>` or `<button>` targeted by the field's
36	  `<label for>`, so `label.control`, `getByLabel` and the existing `aria-*` bindings keep working
37	  (US-04-BR-05, Q-04 constraint, Q-06, §11.1).
38	- D5. Typed date dd/mm/aaaa for every country, independent of the browser locale, stored as ISO;
39	  unreadable text behaves like the former `badInput` (US-04-BR-06, Q-05; US-01-BR-01, AC-09 note).
40	- D6. Disabled days come from the same pure validator, no second implementation (US-04-BR-06).
41	- D7. Panels: popover on wide screens, bottom sheet below 600 px; 44 × 44 px targets; no horizontal
42	  scroll (US-04-BR-11, AC-12, Q-13).
43	- D8. Bundle budgets (`angular.json`: initial 500 kB warning) kept or justified (spec §9).
44	- D9. Testable in jsdom component tests and Playwright e2e by role and label, never by class
45	  (story; spec §11.1).
46	
47	## Considered Options
48	
49	1. **A. `@angular/aria` 22.3.0 for the combobox, listbox and year list, with `@angular/cdk`
50	   22.3.0** for overlay positioning, the calendar dialog (focus trap and return), live
51	   announcements and breakpoints; the calendar grid's date navigation as a pure function.
52	2. **B. `@angular/cdk` 22.3.0 only**: Overlay, `ActiveDescendantKeyManager` (and `cdk/listbox` for
53	   the year list), `Dialog`, `LiveAnnouncer`; the combobox roles, states and key handling wired by
54	   hand around the key manager.
55	3. **C. Angular Material 22.3.0** (`mat-select` / `mat-autocomplete`, `mat-datepicker` with its
56	   multi-year view), restyled to the design system.
57	
58	Building the widgets from scratch is excluded by the story.
59	
60	## Decision Outcome
61	
62	Chosen option: **"A. `@angular/aria` + `@angular/cdk`"**, because `@angular/aria` is stable at
63	22.x (the developer-preview tag was removed in 22.0.0) and implements the APG combobox wiring that
64	option B would have us write by hand (role and states, `aria-activedescendant`, key relay,
65	typeahead, close on focus-out), which is closest to "from scratch" (D1, D2). It works on an
66	`<input>` (editable) and on a `<button>` (select-only), so the labelled element stays a labelable
67	native element (D4). The CDK supplies what `@angular/aria` does not have: overlay positioning with
68	a bottom sheet, a modal dialog with focus trap and return, and the live announcer. Material (C)
69	would bring a complete date picker but a select host that a `<label for>` cannot target and a
70	theming system that competes with our token tiers.

95	#### 3. The custom select
96

101	  threshold): an `<input type="text" ngCombobox>`; typing expands it and writes the filter text.
102	  Either element gets `id="field-<key>"` (input `controlId`), so the existing `<label for>` targets
103	  it. Its accessible name is the label; for the button variant `aria-labelledby` also points at the
104	  label, so the shown value is not folded into the name in any browser.
105	- **Attributes.** `@angular/aria` binds `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`,

109	  explicitly), applied to the focus element.

111	  `focusMode="activedescendant"`, `selectionMode="explicit"`, `[wrap]="false"`; one `ngOption` per
112	  configured option in `sortOrder`, `aria-selected` from the listbox; the selected one shows
113	  `LucideCheck` (hidden) and a style. The prompt "Selecciona una opción" is not an option: it is the
114	  button's text when the value is `''`, and the input's placeholder for a searchable select.
115	- **Behaviour owned by `CustomSelect`** (not provided by `@angular/aria`, each tied to a test row):
116	  Alt+ArrowDown opens on the current option (AC-06); Tab with the list open commits the active
117	  option and lets focus move (AC-06); on a collapsed select-only, a printable key opens and moves to
118	  the first match (AC-06); Escape or leaving a searchable select restores the shown label and clears
119	  the filter without changing the value (AC-07); filtering through `filterOptions()` with the first
120	  match active (Q-11); the result count or the empty text announced politely through the CDK
121	  `LiveAnnouncer` (AC-07, §8.1); a pointer click outside closes without changing the value.
122	- **Panel placement.** A `cdkConnectedOverlay` inside the popup template, anchored to the combobox,
123	  `cdkConnectedOverlayUsePopover="inline"`: in browsers with the Popover API the panel is a native

125	  `createOverlayRef` defaults `usePopover` to `true` when `showPopover` exists;
126	  `FlexibleOverlayPopoverLocation` `'inline'` inserts it next to the trigger). Below

133	#### 4. The date field and the calendar
134	
135	- **Text box.** `<input type="text" inputmode="numeric" id="field-<key>">`, placeholder
136	  "dd/mm/aaaa", hint "Formato: dd/mm/aaaa" first in `aria-describedby`. No input mask.
137	- **Parsing (pure, `date-text.ts`).** `parseDateText(text)` returns `''` for blank text, the ISO
138	  `YYYY-MM-DD` for `d/m/yyyy` with `/`, `-` or `.` separators (1–2 digit day and month) or exactly
139	  8 digits `ddmmyyyy`, and `null` for anything else, including impossible dates (31/04, 29/02 of a
140	  non-leap year) and 2-digit years (Q-05). `formatDateText(iso)` returns `dd/mm/yyyy`. Every AC-08
141	  row is a unit test. The function lives next to the validators and imports nothing from Angular.
142	- **Binding (`transformedValue`).** `DateField` keeps the shown text with Signal Forms'
143	  `transformedValue(value, { parse, format })` (`@publicApi 22.0`, `@angular/forms@22.3.0`
144	  typings). `parse` returns `{ value: iso }`, `{ value: '' }` for blank, and
145	  `{ value: '', error: { kind: 'parse', message: '' } }` for unreadable text, so the stored value
146	  is `''` and the field is invalid through a `parse` error, which Signal Forms reports to the bound
147	  field automatically and which the existing `errorOf()` already maps to the US-01-AC-09 message
148	  rules (no new message). **Verified hazard:** in `@angular/forms@22.3.0`
149	  (`fesm2022/signals.mjs`, `transformedValue`), the raw value is a `linkedSignal(() =>
150	  format(value()))`, so writing `''` to the model would recompute the shown text to `''` and erase
151	  what the person typed (the R1-F03 failure of US-01 in a new form). Therefore `format(iso)` returns
152	  the last typed text whenever that text parses to `iso` (unreadable text parses to `''`), and
153	  `formatDateText(iso)` otherwise. On blur a readable text is normalised to dd/mm/aaaa. A calendar
154	  choice writes the model, and the text follows through `format`. AC-08's empty-`stored` rows prove
155	  it in a component test.
156	- **"Elegir fecha".** A `<button type="button">` after the text box, accessible name
157	  "Elegir fecha: {label}", `LucideCalendarDays` hidden. It is the one new Tab stop (US-04-BR-13).
158	- **Calendar dialog.** Opened with the CDK `Dialog`: `ariaModal: true`, labelled by the visible
159	  month-and-year text (not a heading, US-04-BR-13), `autoFocus` on the day that holds the roving
160	  `tabindex="0"`, focus returned to "Elegir fecha" on close by passing that button as
161	  `restoreFocus` (the CDK default, `restoreFocus = true`, returns to whatever was focused before
162	  opening, verified in `fesm2022/dialog.mjs`; passing the element also covers browsers where a
163	  pointer click does not focus a button), backdrop, `disableAnimations: true`. The CDK dialog marks the siblings of the overlay container `aria-hidden="true"` while

165	  screens: a flexible connected position strategy anchored to the date field; below
166	  `--breakpoint-sheet`: the bottom-sheet strategy of §3.
167	- **Grid.** A `<table role="grid">`, columns Monday first with full day names from
168	  `Intl.DateTimeFormat(<country locale tag>, { weekday: 'long' })`, one `role="gridcell"` per day
169	  with `aria-label` "15 de mayo de 1990" (`{ day, month: 'long', year }`; Node 24 ICU gives exactly
170	  "15 de mayo de 1990" and "mayo de 1990" for es-CO and es-CL), `aria-selected` on the stored day,
171	  `aria-disabled="true"` on disabled days (still reachable with arrows, not choosable). Roving
172	  tabindex. Keys go through the pure `nextFocusDate(date, key, shift)`: arrows ±1 day / ±7 days
173	  crossing months, Home/End to Monday/Sunday of the week, PageUp/PageDown ±1 month clamped to the
174	  month's last day, Shift+PageUp/PageDown ±1 year clamped (29/02/2000 → 28/02/2001), Enter/Space
175	  choose, Escape closes. `@angular/aria`'s `ngGrid` is not used: it moves only inside the rendered
176	  rows (arrows, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/End in `_widget-chunk.mjs`) and has no PageUp/PageDown, so the
177	  calendar would override most keys anyway.
178	- **Year list.** "Elegir año" swaps the grid for an `ngListbox` (`focusMode="roving"`,
179	  `selectionMode="explicit"`, `[wrap]="false"`) of the years of `yearRange()`, the current year
180	  selected; Enter chooses, returns to the grid on the same day and month of the chosen year (clamped).
181	- **Disabled days and range (D6).** `isDayDisabled(config, iso, today)` is
182	  `validateField(config, iso, today) !== null` (the value is never empty, so "required" never
183	  applies). `latestValidDate()` probes backwards from today with the same function;
184	  `yearRange()` is [Y−120, year of the latest valid date] when the field has any rule that
185	  disables days, else [Y−120, Y+10] (Q-12). No `minAge` arithmetic is written twice.
186	
187	#### 5. Signal Forms integration (D3)
188	
189	- `CustomSelect` and `DateField` implement `FormValueControl<string>` (`@publicApi 22.0`): a
190	  required `value = model<string>()`, a `touch` output emitted when focus leaves the whole widget
191	  (control, button, panel), and a `focus()` method that focuses the labelled element. The form
192	  template binds them with the existing narrowing accessor `[formField]="text(config.key)"`; no new
193	  cast (ADR-0004's "two accessors are the only casts" holds).
194	- `focusBoundControl()` calls the control's `focus()` when it is implemented (typings of
195	  `FormUiControl.focus`: "If the focus method is not implemented, Signal Forms will attempt to focus
196	  the host element"), so a failed "Continuar" focuses the combobox or the date text box (AC-10 of
197	  US-01, unchanged).
198	- The components declare **no** inputs named `invalid`, `required`, `touched`, `errors` or
199	  `disabled`: `FormField` auto-binds inputs with those names (`FormUiControl`), which would show
200	  `aria-invalid` before the field is touched. The form passes the shown-error state explicitly.
201	- Stored values: option `value`, ISO date or `''`, as before (ADR-0003, ADR-0004).
202	
203	#### 6. Store writer (amends the ADR-0004 implementation note)
204	
205	`date` keys leave the `nativeKeys` set of `quote-form.ts`: the date model now holds `''` for
206	unreadable text, so the model is the truth and `flushModel()` writes date keys like text and select
207	keys. `syncNative` and `validity.badInput` remain for `number` only.
208	
209	#### 7. Lazy step 1 (D8)
210	
211	Measured on a throwaway copy of `frontend/` (production build, `@angular/build` 22.3.0; baseline
212	initial `main` 381.44 kB raw / 98.94 kB transfer): `@angular/aria` combobox and listbox with CDK
213	overlay, dialog, a11y and layout **+125.40 kB raw / +27.81 kB transfer**; CDK alone **+99.29 /
214	+22.58**. With the icons of ADR-0010, an eager build would pass the 500 kB warning. The
215	`/:country/datos` route therefore uses `loadComponent` for `QuoteFormPage`, so these packages and
216	the step 1 icons load in a lazy chunk. The address, the guards and the "focus the arriving `h1`"
217	rule of ADR-0001 are unchanged; the existing static guard forbids lazy loading only in the summary
218	feature (US-03-AC-03). The budgets of `angular.json` are not changed.
219	
220	#### 8. What tests can and cannot see
221	
222	- **Component tests (jsdom 31.0.1).** jsdom has no `showPopover` and no `inert` (checked in the
223	  installed package), so the CDK falls back to its overlay container under `document.body`: panels
224	  and the calendar render **outside** the component's root. Helpers find them through the
225	  combobox's `aria-controls` (once rendered) or by role in `document`, as spec §11.1 already plans.
226	  The overlay container is torn down between tests.
227	- **E2E (Playwright).** Page-wide role queries are unaffected by where the panel sits. Focus trap,
228	  real key sequences, bottom-sheet geometry and the 44 px boxes are proven here.
229	
230	### Consequences
231	
232	- Good, because the APG combobox wiring comes from a maintained Angular package, not from our code
233	  (D1, D2), and the date logic that is ours is pure and unit-tested row by row.
234	- Good, because the labelled element stays a native `<input>` or `<button>`: `<label for>`,
235	  `label.control`, `getByLabel` and the `aria-*` bindings keep working (D4); §11.1's changes stay
236	  by role and label.
237	- Good, because validation, messages, stored values and the submit focus rule do not change
238	  (D3): `validateField` is still the only rule engine, now also deciding disabled days (D6).
239	- Good, because the bundle stays within budget by moving step 1 to a lazy chunk (D8).
240	- Bad, because `@angular/aria` has been stable only since 22.0.0 (2026-06-03, about five and a half
241	  months) and its combobox was rewritten in that release (legacy combobox removed,
242	  `SimpleCombobox` promoted to `Combobox`, `values` renamed `value`) — mitigation: pinned 22.3.0;
243	  the use is confined to `CustomSelect` and the year list; every keyboard row is a test.
244	- Bad, because `@angular/aria` renders the popup lazily, so `aria-controls` is absent while the
245	  combobox is collapsed, at least until the list has been opened once (host binding `[attr.aria-controls]: _pattern.popupId()`, and the popup
246	  widget registers only when rendered), while WAI-ARIA 1.2 says authors "MUST set aria-controls on a
247	  combobox element to a value that refers to the combobox popup element" — mitigation: the gap is
248	  reported to the spec (*Spec impact* 3) and checked with a screen reader at HC3. `preserveContent`
249	  (an inherited input of `Combobox`) keeps the popup template rendered after the first open, but
250	  the listbox sits inside the CDK overlay's own template, which is detached on close, so the
251	  developer must confirm in a component test whether the reference survives a close; if the human
252	  requires strict conformance, option B can replace `@angular/aria` inside `CustomSelect` without
253	  touching the form.
254	- Bad, because the wrapper still owns several behaviours (Alt+ArrowDown, Tab commit, collapsed
255	  typeahead, Escape restore, filtering, announcements, sheet) — mitigation: each maps to an AC-06/07
256	  row and is tested in both select kinds.
257	- Bad, because the date text needs a custom `format` to keep unreadable text visible (verified
258	  `linkedSignal` hazard) — mitigation: AC-08 rows with an empty `stored` value test exactly this.
259	- Bad, because jsdom cannot show the top layer, `inert` or real focus trapping — mitigation: e2e.
260	- Neutral: two packages of about 3.6 MB (`@angular/cdk`) and 1.2 MB (`@angular/aria`) unpacked in
261	  `node_modules`; only what is imported reaches the bundle.
262	
263	### Strongest argument against
264	
265	Option B (CDK only) builds on the most proven parts of the Angular ecosystem:
266	`ActiveDescendantKeyManager`, `Overlay` and `Dialog` have years of production use, while
267	`@angular/aria` has been stable for under six months, had its combobox rewritten with breaking
268	changes in 22.0.0, has had about two dozen fixes since, leaves `aria-controls` off a collapsed
269	combobox, has no date picker at all, and adds 26 kB raw on top of the CDK. With B every
270	ARIA attribute is ours to set exactly as the APG says, so the `aria-controls` gap does not exist,
271	and there is one primitive library to understand instead of two.
272	
273	**Why we accept it:** under B the combobox's role, states, key relay, typeahead hand-off and
274	close-on-focus-out are hand-written: that is the "from scratch" part the story rules out, and the
275	part where accessibility bugs usually live. `@angular/aria` is the Angular team's implementation of
276	exactly that pattern, its developer-preview tag was removed in 22.0.0, and it peer-pins the same CDK
277	we need anyway. The decision is contained: `@angular/aria` is used only inside `CustomSelect` and
278	the year list, both behind `FormValueControl<string>`, so falling back to B later rewrites one
279	component, not the form. The 26 kB are in a lazy chunk.
280	
281	### Confirmation
282	
283	- Unit tests: `date-text.spec.ts` (every AC-08 row), `calendar-dates.spec.ts` (every AC-09 keyboard
284	  row through `nextFocusDate`, every AC-10 row with a pinned clock, year ranges of AC-10),
285	  `select-search.spec.ts` (AC-07 filters, accents, case).
286	- Component tests: `custom-select.spec.ts` (AC-05, every AC-06 row on "Marca" and on "Tipo de
287	  documento", AC-07, `aria-expanded`, `aria-activedescendant`, `aria-selected`, prompt),
288	  `date-field.spec.ts` (AC-08 including the rows with empty `stored` and text kept, hydration,
289	  AC-09 flow and names, AC-10), `quote-form-page.spec.ts` per §11.1 (failed "Continuar" focuses the
290	  combobox and the date text box through `focusBoundControl()`).
291	- E2E `us-04-design-system.spec.ts`: real keyboard on select and calendar, focus trap and return,
292	  panels at three viewports (AC-12), stored object of AC-11.
293	- Static checks (code-reviewer): `frontend/package.json` pins `@angular/cdk` and `@angular/aria` to
294	  `22.3.0`; `@angular/aria` is imported only by `custom-select.ts` and `calendar.ts`; no
295	  `ReactiveFormsModule`/`FormControl` (ADR-0004 grep unchanged); the only `as unknown as FieldTree`
296	  casts are still the two accessors; `field-validators.ts`, `date-text.ts` and `calendar-dates.ts`
297	  import nothing from `@angular/*`.
298	- HC3: screen reader pass on the select (both kinds), the calendar and the year list (spec §9).
299	
300	## Pros and Cons of the Options
301	
302	### A. `@angular/aria` + `@angular/cdk` (chosen)
303	
304	- Good, because the combobox and listbox follow the APG pattern with library-maintained ARIA and
305	  keyboard wiring; works on `<input>` and `<button>`.
306	- Good, because the CDK covers positioning, popover top layer, bottom sheet, modal focus trap and
307	  return, `aria-hidden` of the page behind, and announcements.
308	- Bad, because the library is young (stable since 22.0.0) and has gaps the wrapper fills.
309	- Bad, because +125.40 kB raw for both packages (measured), hence the lazy step 1.
310	
311	### B. `@angular/cdk` only
312	
313	- Good, because every primitive is long-established; one library; full control of every attribute.
314	- Good, because +99.29 kB raw (measured), 26 kB less than A.
315	- Bad, because the combobox ARIA wiring and key handling are hand-written around the key manager:
316	  more custom accessibility code to get right and to test (story: "not from scratch").
317	- Bad, because `cdk/listbox` expects focus inside the listbox, which does not fit a combobox whose
318	  focus stays on the input; only the year list could use it.
319	
320	### C. Angular Material 22.3.0
321	
322	`@angular/material@22.3.0`, MIT (npm view, 2026-11-21). Not measured.
323	
324	- Good, because `mat-datepicker` is a complete, mature date picker with month and multi-year views
325	  and a pluggable date adapter; `mat-autocomplete` covers the search case.
326	- Bad, because `mat-select`'s focus element is the `<mat-select>` host, a custom element that a
327	  `<label for>` cannot target, so `label.control` and the §11.1 helpers break (D4).
328	- Bad, because Material's own theming (system tokens, density, typography) competes with ADR-0010's
329	  token tiers; restyling to the brief means overriding Material's internal structure.
330	- Bad, because it is the heaviest option and adds a third Angular package family to upgrade.
331	
332	## Amendments to accepted ADRs (explicit; the accepted files are not edited)
333	
334	**ADR-0004** (Accepted 2026-11-20):
335	
336	1. Driver **D7** "Native controls, accessible name, description, required and invalid states, error
337	   announced once" now reads, for `select` and `date` fields only: custom controls built on
338	   `@angular/aria` and `@angular/cdk`, whose labelled element is a native `<input>` or `<button>`
339	   targeted by the field's `<label for>`, with the same accessible name, description, required and
340	   invalid bindings and the same one-time error announcement. `text`, `number` and `checkbox` stay
341	   native.
342	2. The **implementation note** (`adr/README.md`, ADR-0004 row): "`syncNative` is the only writer of
343	   number and date keys" becomes "of number keys"; date keys are written by `flushModel()` from the
344	   model, which holds `''` for unreadable text through `transformedValue` (§4, §6). The submit gate,
345	   `onInvalid` with `focusBoundControl()`, and the `parse`-error message rule are unchanged.
346	
347	If this ADR is accepted, the `adr/README.md` row of ADR-0004 reads "Accepted (amended by ADR-0012)",
348	and the implementation-notes table gets a pointer row.
349	
350	## Spec impact (reported to the orchestrator; the spec is not edited here)
351	
352	1. **§11.1, AC-05 and `expectEmptyStep1`**: for a **searchable** select (an `<input>`), the prompt
353	   "Selecciona una opción" is the placeholder, so `inputValue()` is `''` when empty. Tests of the
354	   empty state should assert the placeholder (or the accessible description) plus the stored value,
355	   not `inputValue() === 'Selecciona una opción'`. For a select-only (a `<button>`), the prompt is
356	   the visible text.
357	2. **US-04-AC-09** "the page behind is inert": the CDK dialog gives a focus trap, a backdrop that
358	   takes pointer events and `aria-hidden="true"` on the page behind, not the HTML `inert`
359	   attribute. The scenario should assert those three (or the developer adds `inert` and the test
360	   checks it in e2e; jsdom has no `inert`).
361	3. **§11.1 `quote-form-page.spec.ts` "select → role=combobox with `aria-expanded="false"` and
362	   `aria-controls`"**: with `@angular/aria`, `aria-controls` is bound only while the list is
363	   rendered; while collapsed it is absent (at least before the first open). Either relax that
364	   assertion to "while expanded" or accept option B for `CustomSelect`.
365	4. **US-04-Q-12 / AC-09 "Monday first"**: CLDR week data (Node 24 ICU, `Intl.Locale.weekInfo`)
366	   gives Sunday as the first day for `es-CO` and Monday for `es-CL`. The spec fixes Monday for both
367	   countries; the human should confirm this is intended for Colombia.
368	5. **US-04-Q-11 with Q-13 on phones**: a searchable select on a 360 px screen opens a bottom sheet
369	   while the on-screen keyboard is up; the sheet must fit above the keyboard. The ADR keeps one
370	   combobox pattern at every width (focus stays in the text box); the HC3 phone pass must check
371	   this, and if it fails, the fallback is a sheet with its own search box (a dialog), which changes
372	   the ARIA pattern on narrow screens and needs a spec change.
373	6. **US-01 supersessions** listed in US-04-Q-04 (Q-22 native date, §9 native controls, BR-02 prompt
374	   as an option) are consistent with this ADR.
375	
376	## More Information
377	
378	- **Verified on 2026-11-21** (npm registry, `npm pack` into a temporary directory, installed
379	  packages in `frontend/node_modules`, and a throwaway build; nothing installed in the project):
380	  - `npm view @angular/aria@22.3.0`: MIT; peers `@angular/cdk 22.3.0`, `@angular/core ^22.0.0 || ^23.0.0`;
381	    published 2026-11-18. Entry points: `accordion`, `combobox`, `grid`, `listbox`, `menu`, `tabs`,
382	    `toolbar`, `tree` (each with `testing`); no date picker.
383	  - `npm view @angular/cdk@22.3.0`: MIT; peers as in §1; deps `tslib`, `parse5`.
384	  - Stability: angular/components `CHANGELOG.md`, release **22.0.0 (2026-06-03)**: "remove developer
385	    preview tag from aria" (#33232) and "promote simple-combobox to stable un-prefixed combobox";
386	    breaking: "The legacy combobox and autocomplete implementations have been removed", "Renames the
387	    values input/model to value in Combobox, Listbox, …". About 24 entries in the `aria` scope from
388	    22.0.1 to 22.3.0 (counted from a summarised read of the CHANGELOG; approximate). The packed
389	    typings carry no stability tags. angular.dev "Angular Aria" overview (site built at v22.3.0):
390	    no stability notice, a "New" label; patterns listed: Autocomplete, Listbox, Select,
391	    Multiselect, Combobox, Menu, Menubar, Toolbar, Accordion, Tabs, Tree, Grid.
392	  - API facts from packed `@angular/aria@22.3.0`: `Combobox` inputs `disabled`, `readonly`,
393	    `softDisabled`, `alwaysExpanded`, `tabindex`, models `expanded`, `value`; `ComboboxPopup`
394	    `popupType` `'listbox' | 'tree' | 'grid' | 'dialog'`; `Listbox` inputs `wrap`, `focusMode`
395	    (`activedescendant` | `roving`), `selectionMode` (`explicit` | `follow`), `typeaheadDelay`,
396	    model `value`; `DeferredContentAware.preserveContent`.
397	  - `@angular/forms@22.3.0`: `FormValueControl`, `FormUiControl` (`touch`, `focus()`),
398	    `transformedValue` and `TransformedValueSignal` are `@publicApi 22.0`; `transformedValue` builds
399	    the raw value with `linkedSignal` (`fesm2022/signals.mjs`).
400	  - jsdom 31.0.1 (`frontend/node_modules/jsdom`): no `showPopover`, no `inert` implementation.
401	  - WAI-ARIA 1.2, combobox role (w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2, read 2026-11-21): required states and
402	    properties `aria-controls`, `aria-expanded`.
403	  - Build measurements: see §7.
404	- **Third-party skill conflict (CLAUDE.md §1, §5):** the vendored `angular-aria.md` says "Never use
405	  native HTML elements like `<select>`" and shows `[formField]` bound directly to `ngCombobox`. We
406	  reach `@angular/aria` on our own drivers, but we do **not** bind `[formField]` to `ngCombobox`:
407	  its `value` model is the input's text (the search string), not the option value, so it would
408	  store labels or filter text. The form binds `CustomSelect`, which maps the listbox selection to
409	  the option value.
410	- **Related ADRs:** ADR-0004 (amended here), ADR-0003 (stored values unchanged), ADR-0001 (route
411	  address unchanged; step 1 lazy), ADR-0010 (tokens, icons, breakpoints), ADR-0013 (panel motion,
412	  `disableAnimations`).
413	- **Revisit when:** `@angular/aria` ships a date picker or changes its combobox API; the HC3 screen
414	  reader or phone pass fails on the select or the calendar; the `aria-controls` gap is judged a
415	  blocker.
